## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mettākathā* ("Discussion of Love") is the fourth chapter of the second division (Yuganaddhavagga) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text presents an extensive and systematic treatment of loving-kindness (*mettā*), opening with a quotation of the *Mettānisaṁsa* discourse found in the Aṅguttara Nikāya, which enumerates the eleven advantages of cultivating love [Sarada Thero]. It provides a detailed exposition of methods for suffusing beings with loving-kindness arranged in numerical order, combining these techniques with the factors of awakening (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*), namely the five faculties (*indriya*), the five powers (*bala*), the seven awakening factors (*bojjhaṅga*), and the noble eightfold path [Sarada Thero].

According to SuttaCentral, related treatments and mentions of this teaching occur in the *Mettāsutta* of the Ekādasakanipāta (AN 11.15), the *Mettāsutta* of the Aṭṭhakanipāta (AN 8.1), the *Ekuttarikanaya* of the Vinaya Parivāra (Pvr 7), and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.4.6) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects substantial Pali-internal text reuse (1,072 matches across 55 texts), sharing extensive passages with other treatises of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*—particularly the *Vimokkhakathā* (Ps 1.5), *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1), and *Indriyakathā* (Ps 1.4)—as well as the first part of the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. High-similarity parallel segments occur notably between the opening section (§1.1–1.6) and AN 11.15, AN 8.1, and Pvr 7, alongside matches in AN 10, AN 6, and the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33) [DharmaNexus]. The commentary (*Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*) and commentaries to the *Khuddakapāṭha*, *Suttanipāta*, and *Jātaka* also share substantial textual material [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages with the Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Daśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā*, the Chinese *Ekottarika-āgama* (T 125), the Tibetan *Ārya-vimala-nāma-dhāraṇī*, and the *Samāhitā Bhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi* [DharmaNexus].
